title: Kouignettes
subtitle: Individual Breton butter cakes with a caramelized sugar and salt crust
excerpt: Kouignettes are individual versions of kouign amann, the Breton caramelized butter cake. A yeasted dough has butter and sugar folded in like rough puff pastry, then is pressed into muffin tins and baked at high heat until the sugar caramelizes into a brittle, glassy crust. They are best eaten warm.
sourceNotes: Kouign amann (pronounced KWEEN ah-MAHN) was created in 1860 in Douarnenez, Brittany, by baker Yves-Rene Scordia. The name means butter cake in Breton. The individual form (kouignette or kouign amann individuel) became popular with the rise of French artisan bakeries from the 2000s. The recipe uses lamination of butter and sugar into a yeasted dough.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Kouignettes are best eaten warm within an hour of baking. The caramel crust softens on standing. They can be refreshed for 5 minutes in a 180 degrees Celsius oven the next day.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Conventional oven, 200 degrees Celsius. Fan oven: 185 degrees Celsius. The caramel will bubble and may smoke slightly; this is normal.

glossaryTerms.definition: The technique of folding cold butter and caster sugar into a yeasted dough in two or three turns, similar to rough puff pastry. During baking, the sugar caramelizes between the layers and the butter creates a flaky structure. Unlike pastry lamination, the dough contains live yeast, which gives additional lift.

content.text: : cold butter and sugar folded into a soft yeasted dough. Work quickly; if the butter warms and the dough becomes greasy, chill for 20 minutes before the next fold. Use Breton sea salt (or any good-quality flaky salt) on top; it balances the sweetness and is not optional.

content.text: Making the dough and first rise
Combine the flour, yeast, and salt. Add the warm water and mix to a smooth dough. Knead for 5 minutes. Cover and leave for 1 hour until doubled.

On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough into a rectangle about 40 x 20 cm. Slice the cold butter into thin slabs and cover two-thirds of the dough rectangle with butter. Scatter 40 g of caster sugar over the butter. Fold the unbuttered third over the middle, then fold the remaining third on top (letter fold). Turn 90 degrees and roll out again. Chill for 15 minutes.
Repeat the letter fold with the remaining 40 g of sugar scattered over the dough. Chill for a further 15 minutes.
Butter the cups of a 12-cup muffin tin generously. Scatter about 2 teaspoons of the remaining caster sugar into each cup.
Roll the dough to about 5 mm thickness. Cut into 12 squares or rounds and press each one into a muffin cup. The dough will be slightly larger than the cup; fold the edges in. Proof for 30 minutes.

Bake at 200 degrees Celsius for 22 to 25 minutes until deep caramel. Leave to cool in the tin for exactly 5 minutes, then invert immediately onto a wire rack. If left longer, the caramel sets solid and glues them into the tin.

The caramel must still be liquid when the kouignettes are turned out. A 5-minute wait lets the tins cool enough to handle but the caramel remains pourable. Too long and they set solid in the tin; the only way out is to return them to the oven for 2 minutes to re-melt the caramel.
